title: ACP: implement Idempotency-Key semantics on all POSTs
description: RFC agentic_checkout §6 (SEP #120): Idempotency-Key MUST be present on every POST (400 idempotency_key_required); same key+same body returns stored response with same status and Idempotent-Replayed: true; same key+different body 422 idempotency_conflict; in-flight 409 idempotency_in_flight + Retry-After; scope to authenticated identity+endpoint; never cache 5xx; retain >=24h; null vs absent are different; no side effects re-executed on replay. Concrete risk today: two concurrent /complete calls both pass !current.checkoutId (server.ts:630) and place two checkouts / charge twice. Implement as middleware over the existing Cache.

title: ACP: no authentication hook (Bearer token required)
description: Authorization: Bearer is REQUIRED on all checkout endpoints (RFC agentic_checkout §3.1, §7). ReactionaryACPServerOptions (reactionary-acp-server.ts:99-122) has no auth hook and no request Signature/Timestamp verification, so anyone with a checkout_session_id can read/complete/cancel it. The acp-session-id header is a reactionary invention, not part of the spec. Add an authenticate(request) option (and optional signature verification) and scope sessions to the authenticated agent. Discovery must stay unauthenticated.

title: ACP: return negotiated capabilities on every checkout session response
description: capabilities is REQUIRED on every CheckoutSession response and on the create request (rfc.capability_negotiation §4.2.1, OpenAPI CheckoutSessionBase.required). At minimum payment and interventions.supported, computed as the intersection with the agent's declared interventions.supported. Request capabilities is write-only. MUST ignore unknown capability values; MUST NOT base security decisions on agent-declared capabilities. If required interventions are not covered, return message code intervention_required with status not_ready_for_payment.

title: ACP: declare payment handlers in capabilities.payment.handlers instead of payment_provider
description: Responses emit the removed payment_provider{provider, supported_payment_methods} (reactionary-acp-server.ts:853, 895-929). Since 2026-01-30 sellers MUST declare capabilities.payment.handlers[] with required id, name (reverse-DNS e.g. dev.acp.tokenized.card), version, spec, requires_delegate_payment, requires_pci_compliance, psp, config_schema, instrument_schemas, config; config MUST include merchant_id and psp (rfc.payment_handlers §5.1, §10). Optional display_name, display_order. Fallback silently advertises 'stripe' even when the backend has no stripe method (server.ts:925), so agents would mint an SPT for a PSP/merchant that cannot charge it. merchant_id is never exposed although agents need it for the delegate_payment allowance. Replace the paymentProvider option with a typed paymentHandlers option.

title: ACP: accept payment_data{handler_id, instrument{type, credential}} on complete
description: ACPPaymentDataSchema (acp-schemas.ts:38-47) still expects the removed {token, provider}. Current shape: payment_data{handler_id, instrument{type, credential{type, token}}, billing_address?} (2026 also allows purchase_order_number/payment_terms for B2B). Seller MUST validate handler_id matches a declared handler (sellers guide). billing_address is parsed but ignored; billing is taken from the shipping address (server.ts:738) - use billing_address when supplied.

title: ACP: buyer schema requires 'name'; spec uses first_name/last_name/email
description: ACPBuyerSchema (packages/acp/src/lib/acp-schemas.ts:8-12) requires 'name'. Every spec version's Buyer uses first_name/last_name/email (2025-09-29..2026-01-16 require all three; 2026-04-17 requires only email and adds full_name, customer_id, account_type, authentication_status, company, loyalty, tax_exemption). A spec-conformant buyer currently gets 400 on create, update and complete. Tests encode the wrong shape (reactionary-acp-server.spec.ts:142, examples/node/src/protocols/acp-e2e.spec.ts:91). Map first/last name to reactionary fields.

title: ACP: replace fulfillment_address/fulfillment_option_id with fulfillment_details/selected_fulfillment_options
description: Breaking change in spec 2025-12-12: fulfillment_address -> fulfillment_details{name, phone_number, email, address{...}}; fulfillment_option_id -> selected_fulfillment_options[{type, option_id, item_ids}]. Our zod z.object schemas (acp-schemas.ts:25-36) strip unknown keys, so a current agent's fulfillment_details and selected_fulfillment_options are silently dropped and the session never reaches ready_for_payment. Responses must also emit the new fields.

title: ACP discovery: 'feeds' is not a valid service
description: getDiscoveryDocument advertises services ['checkout','feeds'] when productFeed is configured (reactionary-acp-server.ts:404). The services enum is closed per API version: checkout, orders, delegate_payment, carts (rfc.discovery §4.2; schema.agentic_checkout.json 2026-04-17). Remove 'feeds'; add 'orders' only once order support exists.

title: ACP: error responses leak internal error details and lack param
description: unwrapACPResult serializes the raw reactionary error into a 400 processing_error (reactionary-acp-server.ts:1203-1215); 500s echo error.message (server.ts:1176). Map reactionary errors to spec Error{type, code, message, param} (e.g. invalid item -> invalid_request, param $.line_items[0].item.id) or session MessageErrors, without leaking internals. processing_error should be a 5xx-class semantic, invalid_request 4xx.

title: ACP: fabricated line-item tax and fulfillment delivery times
description: toACPLineItem hardcodes tax: 0 (reactionary-acp-server.ts:1241) even when the checkout has tax, so line totals do not reconcile with session totals. toACPFulfillmentOption sets tax: 0 and earliest/latest_delivery_time = now() (server.ts:1299-1302). These fields are optional; emit real values or omit them.

title: ACP: minor-unit conversion assumes 2 decimals and clamps negatives
description: toMinorUnits (reactionary-acp-server.ts:1341-1343) multiplies by 100 for every currency: wrong for zero-decimal (JPY, KRW) and three-decimal (KWD, BHD) currencies, and clamps negatives to 0. Use the ISO 4217 exponent (e.g. Intl.NumberFormat(..., {style:'currency', currency}).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits).

title: ACP: payment decline returned as HTTP 400 instead of session message
description: placeCheckout throws 400 processing_error/payment_declined (reactionary-acp-server.ts:772-778). Spec pattern (example checkout_session_with_payment_declined; lifecycle in_progress -> ready_for_payment on failure): return the CheckoutSession (200) with messages[{type:'error', code:'payment_declined', content_type, content}] and status ready_for_payment.

title: ACP: messages[] is always empty; report missing/invalid/out-of-stock conditions
description: messages is hardcoded [] (reactionary-acp-server.ts:874). Lifecycle: not_ready_for_payment must say what is needed. Emit MessageError with code/param/resolution for: missing buyer email or address (missing, $.buyer.email / $.fulfillment_details.address), unknown selected fulfillment option (currently silently ignored at server.ts:811; spec says option_id MUST match an element of fulfillment_options), out_of_stock/low_stock items, backend cart errors. Complete currently returns a generic 400 instead (server.ts:633-639). Use MessageError (2xx) vs Error (4xx) as the spec describes.

title: ACP: emit signed order webhooks (order_create/order_update)
description: RFC agentic_checkout §2.3: order lifecycle events MUST be emitted. POST /agentic_checkout/webhooks/order_events on the agent; header Merchant-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(t + '.' + raw_body, secret)>, 300s replay window; body {type: order_create|order_update, data: full Order (type:'order', id, checkout_session_id, permalink_url, status, line_items, fulfillments, adjustments, totals)} - full object, not deltas (rfc.orders §6). Needs core design for an order-event source and a signing-secret option; align with the UCP order-webhook work (reactionary-dv2). README already lists this as not implemented.

title: ACP: order.permalink_url is emitted as an empty string
description: reactionary-acp-server.ts:870 sets permalink_url: ''. It is required and must be a URI (Order schema). Add an option (URL template with {orderId}) or source it from the backend order.

title: ACP: /complete can return in_progress without an order
description: completeCheckoutSession (reactionary-acp-server.ts:650-672) answers 200 with status in_progress and no order when payment authorization has not arrived within the wait. Spec: complete MUST create an order and return status completed with order (CheckoutSessionWithOrder requires order). Decide a spec-aligned representation for async authorization (2026 status enum includes complete_in_progress) and document it.

title: ACP: fulfillment options use removed subtitle/subtotal/tax/total fields
description: toACPFulfillmentOption (reactionary-acp-server.ts:1288-1305) emits subtitle/subtotal/tax/total. Since 2026-01-16 FulfillmentOptionShipping is {type, id, title, description?, carrier?, earliest_delivery_time?, latest_delivery_time?, totals[]} (required: type, id, title, totals).

title: ACP: line items use pre-2026 flat amounts; add quantity, totals[] and display fields
description: toACPLineItem (reactionary-acp-server.ts:1227-1244) emits flat base_amount/discount/subtotal/tax/total and no top-level quantity. 2026-04-17 LineItem requires id, item, quantity, totals[] (Total{type, display_text, amount}). name, unit_amount and images (available since 2025-12-12) are never emitted although agents render them; product data is available via product.getBySKU.

title: ACP: discovery advertises 2026-01-30 but wire format is 2025-09-29; no API-Version validation
description: ACP_DEFAULT_API_VERSION='2026-01-30' (packages/acp/src/lib/reactionary-acp-server.ts:162) is advertised in /.well-known/acp.json while acp-schemas.ts serves the 2025-09-29 request/response shapes. No API-Version header validation: RFC agentic_checkout §2.1 says client MUST send API-Version, server MUST validate; on missing/unsupported return 400 invalid_request with code unsupported_api_version|missing_api_version and a supported_versions array. Align advertised version with the implemented one (target 2026-04-17) and validate the header.

title: ACP conformance with agenticcommerce.dev spec 2026-04-17 (review 2026-10-05)
description: Review of packages/acp against https://www.agenticcommerce.dev/docs and the canonical spec repo github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol @7fdd78d (latest release 2026-04-17; 2026-01-30 deprecated). The adapter implements a modified 2025-09-29 wire format while discovery advertises 2026-01-30, so current agents fail on create (buyer), lose the address silently and fail on complete (payment data). Missing MUST-level mechanics: Bearer auth, API-Version, Idempotency-Key, order webhooks. Note: the docs site's endpoint examples still show 2025-09-29 shapes; the schema section, RFCs, OpenAPI/JSON Schema and changelogs are authoritative. Wire-format changes are breaking for existing ACP consumers: confirm target version (recommended 2026-04-17 only) before implementing. Each child bead is one review finding.

title: Medusa: pass delegated Stripe credentials to the Stripe payment provider for server-side confirmation
description: Medusa's Stripe provider (medusajs/medusa packages/modules/providers/payment-stripe/src/core/stripe-base.ts, normalizePaymentIntentParameters) forwards payment session data keys payment_method, confirm, off_session, capture_method and shared_payment_token into paymentIntents.create; authorizePayment only reads the intent status. So a delegated token can be confirmed server-side: payment_method=pm_... + confirm=true (manual capture -> requires_capture -> authorized), or shared_payment_token=spt_... for ACP. The reactionary Medusa checkout provider (addPaymentInstructionPayload) passes protocolData through as data verbatim, so UCP's ucp_payment_credential JSON / ACP's delegated_payment_token are ignored and the intent waits for client-side confirmation (punch-out). Map the delegated-token protocol data keys onto those Stripe parameters in the Medusa provider (typed, for provider pp_stripe_stripe), mirroring what the commercetools Stripe API extension does. Note protocolData values are strings (confirm 'true'). Depends on the UCP payment-method resolution bead.

title: UCP: place payments with the backend payment method matching the handler
description: placeFinalCheckout builds the reactionary payment method from the UCP instrument (method = instrument.type e.g. 'card', paymentProcessor = handler id). The Medusa provider uses paymentMethod.method as Medusa's provider_id, so with Medusa every completion fails with 'The payment instruction could not be added' (Medusa's Stripe payment method is method/paymentProcessor 'pp_stripe_stripe'). Resolve the backend payment method via checkout.getAvailablePaymentMethods whose identifier (method or paymentProcessor) matches the instrument's handler id, falling back to today's construction - and verify commercetools keeps working (its static methods are method 'stripe'; today it receives method 'card'). Found running the conformance suite against Medusa (35 passed / 28 failed / 14 skipped; 25 failures are completions).

title: Core: consent management (capability or personalizationProfile extension)
description:
UCP's buyer consent extension (extensions/buyer-consent.md) lets platforms submit buyer consent per purpose (dev.ucp.consent.analytics / marketing / preferences / sale_or_sharing, plus channel segments like marketing.email/sms), each with granted and source (business default vs platform-captured buyer choice). Today the UCP layer only round-trips it on the checkout session (not persisted, extension not advertised).

Decide between a dedicated consent-management capability or extending PersonalizationProfileCapability (currently read-only: getPersonalizationProfile with segments/blurb) with typed get/record-consent mutations and schemas. Implement in the CDP-backed providers (unomi; fake; commercetools/medusa/hcl as applicable).

Record provenance with each decision for GDPR accountability (when, how, for what): e.g. captured via UCP, the platform's agent profile, the checkout session, timestamp - as typed fields, not a free-form bag. Then: persist consent on checkout create/update/complete, advertise dev.ucp.shopping.buyer_consent with the business defaults (source: business) in responses.

title: commercetools: cart/checkout factory price breakdown (totalProductPrice, line discounts)
description: Found while mapping UCP discounts: (1) CommercetoolsCartFactory sets totalProductPrice = totalPrice - shipping, i.e. the product total AFTER discounts (and including tax for net-priced projects), while UCP needs the undiscounted subtotal - the UCP layer now derives it from line items as a workaround. Decide and document the core semantics of CostBreakDown.totalProductPrice (before or after discounts?) and align all providers. (2) parseCartItem adds lineItem.price.discounted.value.centAmount (the discounted PRICE) to totalDiscount, which overstates line discounts when product discounts apply; it should add price.value - price.discounted.value per unit. Check the checkout and order factories for the same.

title: commercetools: include automatic cart discounts in Cart.appliedPromotions
description: Cart.appliedPromotions is meant to list every promotion applied to the cart, with isCouponCode=false for automatic ones and true for user-entered codes. The commercetools cart factory (packages/commercetools/src/factories/cart/cart.factory.ts) only maps cart.discountCodes, so automatic cart discounts (applied when items are added) are missing. Map the cart discounts referenced by lineItems[].discountedPricePerQuantity[].discountedPrice.includedDiscounts and discountOnTotalPrice.includedDiscounts (expand the cart discount references for name/description), de-duplicated, as isCouponCode=false entries - and distinguish code-triggered cart discounts (requiresDiscountCode) so they are not listed twice. Check the checkout factory too.

title: Core: Promotion.amount as the actual monetary amount discounted by each promotion
description: PromotionSchema (packages/core/src/schemas/models/price.model.ts) has an optional amount, described as 'if applicable/available from the source system'; the commercetools factory never sets it. Make it the actual monetary amount discounted by that promotion/adjustment on this cart (summed over line items and the cart total), populated by every provider (commercetools, medusa, magento, hcl, fake), and consider making it required. Consumer: the UCP discount extension's discounts.applied[].amount and allocations, which today fall back to aggregate line/cart discounts. Core schema change - needs clearance; implement in all providers.

title: Core: typed order-callback info on cart/checkout capability (discuss first)
description:
Add provider-neutral metadata to carts and cart items, following the PaymentInstruction.protocolData pattern ({key, value} strings, round-tripped by providers).

Core: Cart.metadata and CartItem.metadata; optional metadata on cart.add, plus cart.setMetadata / cart.setItemMetadata mutations. Checkout and Order expose what they inherit from the cart.

commercetools: a JSON custom field on the cart type (like reactionaryProtocolData on payments) and a line-item custom type; commercetools orders inherit cart and line-item custom fields, so the data reaches the order and the OMS natively. Other providers: map onto their equivalent (e.g. Medusa metadata).

First consumer: UCP order webhooks. Order updates (shipped, delivered, refunds) are known to the backend/OMS, not reactionary, which only captures the order. On completion, UCP would write ucp_order_webhook_url (from the platform's agent profile, order capability config.webhook_url - one URL per platform), ucp_agent_profile and ucp_checkout_session_id, so the OMS can post signed order-updated events itself (it needs the business signing key; see signatures.md). Reactionary keeps sending only the 'Order created' event.

Changes the core schemas - additive, but check clearance for provider implementations.
notes: MUST BE DISCUSSED BEFORE EXECUTION. Design constraint: reactionary avoids any-typed / free-form calls, so an untyped key/value metadata bag is likely not acceptable as proposed. Preferred direction: dedicated, strongly typed capability methods, each with its own mutation and mutation schema, to record order-event callback information (webhook URL, platform profile, originating checkout session) - on the core cart capability, or on the checkout capability if it only matters at checkout. Must then be implemented in every provider (commercetools, medusa, magento, hcl, fake, ...). Revisit whether per-item metadata is still needed under that design.

title: UCP: decide policy for raw card (PAN) credentials on non-test handlers
description: completeCheckoutSession forwards any instrument credential verbatim into the payment's ucp_payment_credential protocol data, which commercetools persists in the reactionaryProtocolData custom field until the payment extension replaces it. A raw card credential (type 'card', card_number_type fpan, number/cvc) would therefore be stored in commercetools - a PCI scope concern. Decide whether to reject raw card credentials unless a handler explicitly opts in, or document it. Behaviour change for consumers - needs clearance before changing.
close_reason: Raw card credentials (pan/card, or carrying number/cvc) are refused with payment_failed and never forwarded, unless acceptRawCardCredentials is set; the harness advertises token-only request_constraints on the Stripe handler. Spec: credentials are opaque tokens, not raw PANs; pan_credential is source-only.

Add a typed rejection reason (a dedicated error type/enum in the mutation result, no free-form data) and map it in every provider. commercetools has the information: addDiscountCode errors and cart.discountCodes[].state (NotActive, NotValid, DoesNotMatchCart, MaxApplicationReached, ApplicationStoppedByPreviousDiscount) - note a code can be accepted onto the cart yet not match it, which today still shows as applied. notes: Rescoped (per discussion): backends generally cannot say WHY a code was rejected, so the UCP code stays discount_code_invalid - no typed reason enum. Instead: an optional free-form, human-readable reason string on the applyCouponCode rejection (still a typed field, not an any-bag), passed through as the UCP warning content. Providers fill it when they know something (e.g. commercetools discountCodes[].state such as DoesNotMatchCart / MaxApplicationReached; also catches codes accepted onto the cart that do not actually apply). Low priority.

title: UCP: guest orders are not visible after OAuth2 identity linking
description: An order placed as a guest is readable only from the placing session/platform. commercetools login (CommercetoolsAPI.login) does not sign in with the guest's anonymousId, so after the buyer links their account (OAuth2 identity linking) in a later session, /me/orders does not return orders they placed as a guest before linking. Decide whether login should assign anonymous orders to the customer (commercetools sign-in with anonymousId) - affects all reactionary consumers, not just UCP.
notes: Not required: orders placed while OAuth2-linked are readable from later OAuth2 sessions (verified live). This only covers guest orders placed before linking.

value: In the Docker sandbox, origin is an SSH remote that cannot authenticate; push with: git push https://github.com/Solteq/reactionary.git <branch>, then git fetch https://github.com/Solteq/reactionary.git <branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch> and set upstream to origin/<branch>. Requires 'sbx secret set github --sandbox ReactionarySandbox -t $(gh auth token)' on the host. bd is installed via npm i -g @beads/bd (v1.3.1). Running the UCP conformance suite: examples/node/conformance/run-ucp-conformance.sh (Docker) on a dev machine. In the Docker sandbox, docker build cannot reach apt and node_modules are darwin-only, so the suite was run natively instead: git clone Universal-Commerce-Protocol/conformance, drop [tool.uv.sources] ucp-sdk from pyproject, uv sync, copy examples/node/conformance/{conformance_input.json,test_fixtures.json,payment_instruments.csv,addresses.csv} into test_data/flower_shop, start the server from a separate Linux pnpm install (copy of the repo without node_modules) with the env the run script exports, export SIMULATION_SECRET for both server (UCP_TEST_SIMULATION_SECRET) and pytest, then SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787 uv run pytest. Completion takes ~4s from the sandbox, close to the suite's 5s client timeout.

UCP design decisions agreed with Asger: test-only behaviour lives behind explicit opt-in server options with warning banners (anonymousOrderEmail, testPaymentHandlers, testOrderUpdates, testSimulationSecret, webhooks.allowInsecureUrls); follow the UCP spec over the conformance suite where they disagree (items_discount vs discount, reactionary-lf7); no shared commercetools test-data changes without asking; reactionary avoids any-typed/free-form calls - new data (e.g. order-callback info reactionary-dv2, consent reactionary-0sn) needs typed capability methods + mutation schemas in all providers, discussed first; order updates (shipping) should ultimately come from the backend/OMS, reactionary only captures orders; raw card numbers are never forwarded unless acceptRawCardCredentials.
